subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should an experimental Claw be allowed to install process-wide plugins, or should the first package slice support only agent-local skills until an explicit shared-host grant or per-agent plugin scope exists?
rationale: Plugins execute in the shared runtime and can affect sibling agents, while skills live in the role workspace; code review cannot choose that isolation and authorization boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship skills first
options.body: Implement and prove workspace-local skill installation now, keeping plugin actions blocked until a shared-host grant model is approved.

options.title: Require host-level grant
options.body: Keep plugin support only when the consented plan marks process-wide scope and obtains explicit Scout or operator authorization.

options.title: Accept global plugin scope
options.body: Treat normal Claw consent as sufficient authorization for shared plugin installation and document the cross-agent impact.

recommendation.title: Ship skills first
recommendation.body: Implement and prove workspace-local skill installation now, keeping plugin actions blocked until a shared-host grant model is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the assigned reviewer with the strongest direct evidence on package ownership, trust ordering, and the adjacent skill lifecycle.
